## Why this matters

Every LLM serving system spends most of its latency budget on
autoregressive decoding, and almost every decoding optimization — from
speculative decoding to paged attention — is really an optimization on
top of one core mechanism: the KV-cache. Understanding what the cache
stores and how it grows is a prerequisite for reasoning about inference
cost at all [@src-10; @src-11].

A decode step's cost is dominated by reading the existing cache, not by
recomputing it:

$$
\text{decode\_step\_cost} \approx \underbrace{c_{\text{qkv,1 tok}}}_{\text{small, fixed}} + \underbrace{c_{\text{read}}(n)}_{\text{grows with cache length } n}
$$ {#eq-decode-cost}

::: {.callout-note title="Analogy"}
Think of the KV-cache like a sign-in sheet at a long meeting. Prefill is
everyone already in the room signing in at once. Each new person who
walks in later (a decode step) only has to read the *existing* sheet and
add *one* new line — they never re-collect everyone's signatures from
scratch. The sheet only ever grows by one line per new arrival.
:::

## Visual overview

![Prefill builds the whole KV-cache from the prompt in one pass; each
decode step afterward reads the entire cache but appends exactly one new
K/V slot to it.](../../figures/rendered/kv_cache_demo.svg){#fig-kv-cache}

::: {.callout-warning title="Common misconception"}
A common misconception is that the model "re-reads the whole prompt"
before producing each new token during decoding. It does not: the prompt
is processed once, during prefill. Every later decode step reuses the
cached K/V projections from that single prefill pass and only computes
fresh K/V for the one new token being generated.
:::

## Compare and contrast

| Aspect | Prefill | Decode step |
|---|---|---|
| Tokens processed per pass | All prompt tokens at once | Exactly 1 new token |
| KV-cache slots created | 1 per prompt token | 1 (appended to existing cache) |
| Dominant cost driver | Compute (large matmul over the whole prompt) | Memory bandwidth (reading a growing cache) |

: What changes between the prefill pass and a single decode step {#tbl-prefill-vs-decode}

## Check your understanding

1. During autoregressive decoding, does the KV-cache store the attention
   *output* for each past token, or the key/value *projections* for each
   past token?
2. A prompt has 4 tokens and the model generates 3 new tokens one at a
   time. After prefill and all 3 decode steps, how many K/V slots does
   the cache hold, and how many *new* slots did each individual decode
   step add?

answer records (`q-04-kv-cache-001`, `q-04-kv-cache-002`).
